The '''Que Desert''', also known as the West Mahean Desert, the Crulat steppe, the Que Steppe, desert, semi-desert, and steppe, covering about 1,135,770 square kilometres (705,735 square miles) of [[West Mahea]]. To the south, it borders and merges into the [[Liaax Highlands]]. The land is hilly, rocky, or gravelly desert, cut with occasional wadis, or river valleys, which are generally dry riverbeds. To the north, it borders the [[Okaren Mountains|Okaren Mountain range]].
===Location and name===
The desert is bounded by the [[Sliect]] to the west, and by the [[Serenr Steppe]] to the east. In the south, the desert gives way to the more fertile areas and to the north it runs into the [[Okaren Mountains]].

Several parts of the Que Desert have been referred to separately, such as the Taoisian desert around [[Taoisia]], and the Haeu desert. The southern section of the desert, that within the borders of [[Trian]], can be referred to (within the  Trian context) as the Northern Desert.
The name Qyan has also been used for the Qun Desert. The name has been translated in the past as Wi-Slaio-aq or Wo-Slaio-aq
[[File:Fonds Raymonde Bonnefille - Ethiopie, Hadar - Mission 1973 - Paysage d'Hadar vu d'un point de vue élevé (MédiHAL 5358235).jpg|left|thumb|This photograph illustrates the vastness of the Que Desert. Taken from a high altitude, it reveals mountains in the background. At their base, a thin strip of verdant vegetation borders the landscape. The rest of the terrain is composed of sparse sandy soil. No villages are visible.]]

===Geography===
The 1000–1200-metre high region in the middle of the desert is the [[Samna Plateau]], a rather flat, stony [[Wikipedia:Semi-arid_climate|semi-desert]] consisting of [[Wikipedia:Limestone|limestone]] bedrock covered with chert gravel. What little rain arrives on the plateau flows into local [[Wikipedia:Salt_pan_(geology)|salt flats]]. The highest peaks of the plateau are those of the 1,200m+ [[Khioaskaz Ual]] in [[Taoisia]], and the 1,300-metre-high [[Tohuzb Ual]]. at the border of [[Taoisia]] and [[Sivoso]].
